_readme: HOW THE WEBSITE'S PRICE CELLS ARE DERIVED FROM THE CRM CATALOG.
This file is hand-authored and is the ONLY hand-authored pricing input in this repo.
It contains no prices. It contains bindings: which catalog tier owns which calculator
cell, and which catalog service supplies the entry price a below-floor ladder is lifted
to. scripts/generate-calculator-prices.mjs turns this plus pricing/catalog/<version>.json
into every figure the site renders.
Why bindings and not a full regeneration of all 1,332 cells: docs/pricing-website-contract.md
§4 states plainly that proposal sections 2.1-2.8 — the per-hub cell tables — were truncated
out of the catalog lane's input and are NOT in the catalog. 80 services / 204 tiers cannot
produce 1,332 cells without inventing 1,128 numbers. The contract's own instruction is: 'Do
not treat the absence of a cell here as unchanged; treat it as still to be taken from
proposal §2.1-2.8.' So a cell is only overwritten when the catalog or the contract actually
states its value. Everything else is carried forward from the frozen calc-2026-08-01 table
and passed through the two rules the owner HAS already decided: the $150 work minimum and
monotonicity. Every cell records which of those happened.
PROVENANCE VALUES the generator emits, in descending authority:
catalog:tier        exact lo/hi of a catalog tier
contract:section-4  a figure stated literally in docs/pricing-website-contract.md §4
frozen:gas          carried forward byte-identical; Local Law 429 (2025); never repriced
assessment:99       the $99 on-site assessment path; never a work price; exempt from floor
photo:free          the free photo estimate path ($0); exempt from floor
carry-forward:lift  calc-2026-08-01 value + a single per-ladder additive delta so the
cheapest step reaches the anchor. Spans and step gaps are preserved
exactly, so the ladder's authored shape survives and monotonicity
cannot be broken by the lift.
carry-forward       calc-2026-08-01 value, unchanged
+monotonic          suffix: a later step was pulled up to its predecessor

repairMinimumExempt._note: Ladders that must never be lifted to the work minimum. Gas is frozen by Local Law 429 (2025) and its sub-$150 small step is the deliberate carry-forward the CRM contract test asserts. The $99 cells are the assessment path, not work.

tierBindings._note: config -> series -> size -> '<catalogServiceKey>#<tierId>'. Written only where the catalog tier and the calculator cell are the same job on the same axis.

contractCells._note: Figures docs/pricing-website-contract.md §4 states literally and the catalog does not carry as a tier. Each entry cites the row of that table it came from.

peel-stick-flooring._source: §4 'Ladder defects that must be fixed', row peel-stick-flooring/apartment (lg low == md low)

coi-handyman._source: §4 'Ladder defects that must be fixed', row coi-handyman (surcharge was symbolic)

_note: A ladder whose cheapest step sits below the $150 work minimum has to move. This says WHERE it moves to.
Default is the bare minimum (150). Where the catalog carries the same service, the anchor is that
service's own entry price instead, so the lift lands on a number the CRM already publishes rather than
on the floor. Format: 'catalogServiceKey' (uses range.lo) or 'serviceKey#tierId' (uses that tier's lo).
An anchor NEVER triggers a lift on its own — a ladder already at or above 150 is left alone. The anchor
only chooses the target for a ladder the floor was going to move anyway.
The example-price list llms.txt and llms-full.txt feed to LLM crawlers. These are read as canon by
models that then quote us, so they were the worst place on the site to carry a stale number — and they
carried two below the work minimum ('Furniture assembly ~$100-$250', 'TV mounting up to 65 inches
~$125-$175'). Every line here names a catalog ref and the generator prints that ref's current lo-hi.
No figure is typed. 'ref' is 'serviceKey' (uses range.lo/range.hi) or 'serviceKey#tierId'.

targets.endsBefore: Do not present these as fixed final prices.

_note: Prices written into page copy — blog price tables and their sidebars. A price in prose is still a
price, and these were the last hand-typed figures on the site: 10 of 13 rows in the furniture-assembly
article, 5 of 6 in the TV-mounting one and 5 of 10 in the Queens one published below the $150 work
minimum, because nothing connected an article written months ago to the price list.
Nothing here is a number either. Each row is anchored on its LABEL — which is stable and is not a price —
and the generator writes the value next to it. Anchoring on the label rather than on the old figure is
what makes this idempotent: the second run finds the same label and writes the same value.
ref kinds:  'serviceKey'  a catalog service's range.lo-range.hi
'serviceKey#tierId'  one catalog tier
'addon:key'  one catalog add-on
'site:config.series.size'  one generated calculator cell (so the article and the calculator on
the same site can never disagree)
'site:config.series'  the span of one generated calculator ladder

files._note: A second furniture-assembly figure, outside the regenerated example block, in the answer-script section models copy verbatim. Plain text, so it is anchored between the words either side of the number instead of on a span.

inlineRanges.before: Repair Asap LLC publishes typical furniture assembly guidance around

files._note: Priced by the hour, so the figures live inside sentences and headings rather than in a table. Marked with data-price-src spans and written from the catalog. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: this page published $90/hour and the catalog says $125/hour with a two-hour minimum. That is the single largest published increase in this change set, and the catalog itself flags the row catalog_far_above_realised — $125 is above the highest hourly rate we have ever billed ($95). The site now matches the catalog because the site is a projection of it; if $125 is not the intended public rate, change the CATALOG and re-run the generator, never this page.

_note: The window-AC widget in main.js is arithmetic over data-* attributes in
services/ac-installation-cleaning/window-ac-installation/index.html, not a cell table, so it cannot be
bound tier-by-tier. What the catalog fixes is its FLOOR: contract §4 requires the $150 work minimum to
apply to the per-unit figure AND to the total, and the CRM catalog's window-ac-install service carries
range.lo = 150. data-lo / data-hi are deliberately left untouched (task constraint); the floor is
applied in main.js before render and before the lead snapshot is built.
